Definition: What proportion of businesses does the register cover?
Comments: No specific proportion found; formal sector only, informal excluded.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No source was originally cited; original score unsupported. CEPICI's Annuaire IDU (2025) reports just over 200,000 businesses formally registered (RCCM/CNPS/tax ID) nationally, while ANStat's ongoing national business census (RGEE-CI, 2025) counted roughly 1.2-1.4 million formal and informal economic units. That implies formal-register coverage of the total business population of only ~14-17%, i.e. under 20%, so the code is lowered from 2 to 1. Denominators are approximate (census still provisional) so this should get a light human check.

Definition: What proportion of the intended beneficiaries does the register cover?
Comments: Low coverage of poor households (<20% est.).
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original claim of <20% coverage is contradicted by current official data. The Registre Social Unique (RSU), run by the Ministry of Solidarity's Bureau de Coordination des Programmes Filets Sociaux, had registered over 1.45 million households (8.8 million individuals) as of August 2025, against an official 2021-2025 targeting objective of 'more than 2 million' poor/vulnerable households (Ministry announcement, Jan 2023). That is roughly 70-75% of the intended target population, so the code is raised from 1 to 4 (70-89%). Both sources are the responsible ministry/programme's own publications; figures are self-reported administrative data rather than an independent survey, so some downward caution is warranted.

Definition: What proportion of businesses does the register cover?

revision_notes: No source was originally cited. Côte d'Ivoire's one-stop shop (CEPICI/GUFE) issues a single identifier covering RCCM, tax number (NCC) and CNPS registration together, so business-tax registration tracks the business register closely: roughly 200,000 businesses hold a tax ID against an estimated 1.2-1.4 million total formal and informal economic units counted by the 2024-25 RGEE-CI census, i.e. under 20% of the total business population is captured. A 2021 DGI statement citing only ~130,000 taxpayers subject to non-property taxes nationally supports a small formal base. Code lowered from 3 to 1 for consistency with the business register coverage finding; flagged for light human review given the imprecision of the informal-sector denominator.

Definition: What proportion of individual taxpayers does the register cover?
Comments: No specific data; low formal income tax coverage assumed.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No source was originally cited, but the assumed score is confirmed by evidence. A Directorate-General of Taxes statement (Q3 2021, reported by Abidjan.net) put the total taxpayer base (all non-property taxes) at only around 130,000, a ratio of about 1 taxpayer per 125 residents, explicitly noted by the DGI as low versus regional peers. The e-impots online portal had registered only 74,000 adherents by March 2022. Given Côte d'Ivoire's very large informal/wage-earning population, the individual/income taxpayer base captured is well under 20% of the eligible population. Code confirmed at 1, now evidenced rather than assumed.
